cur-fossil-koro-toro.dateNote: In January 1995 Michel Brunet's French–Chadian team found a jawbone in the Djurab desert of Chad. Named Australopithecus bahrelghazali, it is about 3.5 million years old: the first australopith found west of the Rift Valley. Pinned on the town of Koro Toro; the find site, KT 12, is nearby.
cur-fossil-koro-toro.summary: The first early human relative found in Central Africa, far west of the Rift Valley.

cur-fossil-toros-menalla.dateNote: On 19 July 2001 Ahounta Djimdoumalbaye, of Michel Brunet's French–Chadian team, found a skull in the Djurab desert of northern Chad. Named Sahelanthropus tchadensis, it is about 7 million years old.
cur-fossil-toros-menalla.summary: A 7-million-year-old skull from Chad, one of the oldest possible human relatives.
